name: Maku'a
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.quote: We have attested that stress may shift from the penultimate syllable to the ultimate when encliticised with the NP marker -va, e.g. [hákɛ ⇒ hakɛ́βa ⇒hák̢ɛβa].
new_statements.citation: van Engelenhoven, Aone. 2010. The Makuva Enigma: Locating a Hidden Language in East Timor. Revue Roumaine de Linguistique LV(2): 161-181.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress falls on the penultimate syllable of the lexical word (hákɛ 'pig'); when the noun-phrase enclitic =va is attached, stress moves rightward to the stem's final syllable, which is the penult of the enclitic-extended form (hakɛ́βa), a form which may then be realised with consonant gemination and stress back on the stem's first syllable (hák̢ɛβa). The penultimate default is stated only implicitly ('shift from the penultimate syllable') in a footnote of a grammar sketch reconstructed from fieldwork notes.
new_statements.exceptions: Enclitic =va shifts stress; the third variant [hák̢ɛβa] (geminate k, stress on the antepenult of the enclitic form) shows the shift is not obligatory or interacts with gemination; the author says the gemination rules need further research.
new_statements.domain_note: Lexical word (elicited citation forms from the last speakers, Mehara/Lovaia, fieldwork 2003-2008); shift described at the level of the noun stem plus NP enclitic. Language nearly extinct; data from a handful of elderly bilingual (Fataluku) speakers.
new_statements.identity_note: Source uses the name Makuva (= Glottolog Maku'a maku1277, ISO lva; also Lóvaia/Lovaia, Loikera). Data from the last elderly speakers in Mehara/Lovaia (Tutuala subdistrict), all bilingual in Fataluku; van Engelenhoven treats it as a single language with no dialect division. No other glottocode involved.

sources.note: §2 'Phonotactics and phonology' (pp. 163-166) gives consonants, vowels, metathesis, gemination; the only stress remark is fn. 11 (p. 166): stress may shift from the penultimate to the ultimate syllable of the stem when the NP enclitic -va is added, e.g. [hákɛ ⇒ hakɛ́βa ⇒ hák̢ɛβa] — i.e. default penultimate stress implied, with enclitic-conditioned shift.

sources.note: §3 'Makuva sound changes' (pp. 429-436) gives the phoneme inventory (5 vowels, no long vowels, variable mid-vowel height) and PMP reflexes; nothing on stress or accent (grep for stress/accent/prosod: no hits).
